claims.title: Copán settled
claims.summary: A small farming village on the Copán River grows over centuries into a major Maya centre in what is now western Honduras.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1000bce-copan-settled, claim TL:HND:event:1000bce:copan-settled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dynasty of sixteen kings
claims.summary: A line of at least sixteen rulers governs Copán, raising temples, stelae, and the Hieroglyphic Stairway during the city's Classic-period height.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-426-dynasty-of-sixteen-kings, claim TL:HND:event:426:dynasty-of-sixteen-kings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hieroglyphic Stairway completed
claims.summary: The fifteenth ruler finishes the great stairway, whose roughly 1,200 carved glyphs form the longest known Maya inscription.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-755-hieroglyphic-stairway-completed, claim TL:HND:event:755:hieroglyphic-stairway-completed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Copán abandoned
claims.summary: After centuries of decline the Maya completely abandon Copán, leaving its monuments to the forest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1200-copan-abandoned, claim TL:HND:event:1200:copan-abandoned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Columbus reaches Honduras
claims.summary: On his fourth voyage Christopher Columbus makes landfall on the Caribbean coast of Honduras.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1502-columbus-reaches-honduras, claim TL:HND:event:1502:columbus-reaches-honduras, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lempira's resistance
claims.summary: The Lenca chief Lempira unites more than two hundred communities against the Spanish before his revolt is crushed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1537-lempira-s-resistance, claim TL:HND:event:1537:lempira-s-resistance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Silver strike and rise of Tegucigalpa
claims.summary: A highland silver discovery draws prospectors and gives rise to Tegucigalpa, long a rival to Comayagua.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: The provinces of the Captaincy General of Guatemala, Honduras among them, declare their independence from Spain.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Honduras

claims.title: Federal Republic of Central America
claims.summary: After a brief Mexican annexation, Honduras joins the United Provinces of Central America under a federal constitution adopted in 1824.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Honduras
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Morazán leads the federation
claims.summary: The Honduran Liberal Francisco Morazán serves as president of the United Provinces, fighting to preserve the union against Conservative revolts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1830-morazan-leads-the-federation, claim TL:HND:event:1830:morazan-leads-the-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Honduras becomes sovereign
claims.summary: Amid the federation's collapse, Honduras separates to become a fully independent state.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Honduras

claims.title: Rise of the fruit companies
claims.summary: U.S. firms, foremost United Fruit and Standard Fruit, develop the north coast, making bananas Honduras's dominant export.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1899-rise-of-the-fruit-companies, claim TL:HND:event:1899:rise-of-the-fruit-companies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cuyamel and the Zemurray coup
claims.summary: Samuel Zemurray's Cuyamel Fruit Company buys plantation land and, in 1911, backs an armed coup to secure a favourable government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1910-cuyamel-and-the-zemurray-coup, claim TL:HND:event:1910:cuyamel-and-the-zemurray-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: United Fruit absorbs Cuyamel
claims.summary: Zemurray sells Cuyamel to the United Fruit Company, concentrating the Honduran banana industry as the Depression begins.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1929-united-fruit-absorbs-cuyamel, claim TL:HND:event:1929:united-fruit-absorbs-cuyamel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carías dictatorship
claims.summary: Tiburcio Carías Andino governs as authoritarian president, opening an era of military influence over Honduran politics.

claims.title: War with El Salvador
claims.summary: A brief border war with El Salvador, rooted in migration disputes, erupts amid a football tournament and hardens the military's role.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1969-war-with-el-salvador, claim TL:HND:event:1969:war-with-el-salvador, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Contra war staging ground
claims.summary: Honduras hosts an expanded U.S. military presence at Soto Cano and serves as a base for the Nicaraguan Contras against the Sandinistas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1983-contra-war-staging-ground, claim TL:HND:event:1983:contra-war-staging-ground, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hurricane Mitch
claims.summary: One of the deadliest Atlantic hurricanes devastates Honduras, killing some 7,000 people and ruining infrastructure and crops.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-1998-hurricane-mitch, claim TL:HND:event:1998:hurricane-mitch, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Removal of President Zelaya
claims.summary: The military removes President Manuel Zelaya and Congress installs Roberto Micheletti; a later OAS commission deems the removal an illegal coup while finding Zelaya had defied the courts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-2009-removal-of-president-zelaya, claim TL:HND:event:2009:removal-of-president-zelaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Xiomara Castro inaugurated
claims.summary: Xiomara Castro takes office as Honduras's first woman president, ending years of National Party rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-2022-xiomara-castro-inaugurated, claim TL:HND:event:2022:xiomara-castro-inaugurated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Extradition of Juan Orlando Hernández
claims.summary: Former president Juan Orlando Hernández is extradited to the United States to face drug-trafficking charges, later resulting in conviction.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Honduras: From the Maya kingdom of Copán and the Lenca resistance to a Central American republic shaped by federation, fruit companies, and democratic struggle.", terralore.co/country/HND/chronicle#ev-2022-extradition-of-juan-orlando-hernandez, claim TL:HND:event:2022:extradition-of-juan-orlando-hernandez, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Asfura succeeds Castro
claims.summary: After a narrow, contested 2025 election, Nasry Asfura of the National Party is inaugurated president, succeeding Xiomara Castro.
